did_you_know.text: Did you know? The verse says that the Lord will pour out his Spirit on “all flesh”—an expression emphasizing the broad scope of the vision and the participation of many people in it.
Did you know? The younger generation is described as prophesying, while the older men will dream dreams and the young men will see visions.
Did you know? The vision is not limited by status or gender: it includes both male and female servants, on whom the Lord’s Spirit will be poured out.
Did you know? The repetition of the phrase “I will pour out my Spirit” in verses 1–2 emphasizes that the Spirit’s influence is intended for many groups in society.
Did you know? Before the day of the Lord, signs are described in both the heavens and on earth: blood, fire, and columns of smoke.
Did you know? The description “the sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood” portrays a dramatic change in the heavenly lights before the coming of the great and awesome day of the Lord.
Did you know? According to the verse, everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will escape; calling on the Lord’s name is thus presented as connected with deliverance.
Did you know? Mount Zion and Jerusalem are presented as places where there will be deliverance, and the verse also mentions the survivors whom the Lord calls.
